newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS - Portugal Telecom ties the knot with Concert.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Portugal Telecom ties the knot with Concert.

text.p: Profitable state-controlled telephone operator Portugal Telecom ended the long suspense over its international alliances on Monday, saying it was linking up with the Anglo-American venture, Concert.

Concert is dominated by British Telecom and the U.S. MCI and the companies made clear that the deal with Portugal Telecom was aimed principally at strengthening operations in Latin America, where Portugal has historic links.

"We are delighted with the outcome of the process," said Portugal Telecom chairman Francisco Murteira Nabo. "(We) will work together to create additional business opportunities world-wide and particularly in Brazil," he said.
British Telecom and MCI will take stakes of one percent and 0.5 percent respectively in Portugal Telecom to seal the deal but the Portuguese will not be buying shares in their new partners.
"Portugal Telecom is an ideal strategic partner for MCI and BT," MCI said in a statement issued by Portugal Telecom.

Despite the fact the alliance had been widely predicted, Portugal Telecom shares rose on Monday on the Lisbon bourse, against the negative overall trend, gaining 22 escudos to 6,122 escudos in heavy trade of over 700,000 shares.

Although Portugal is only a small telecommunications market, Concert will gain from the fact that it is growing rapidly and from the country's strategic position in linking Europe and Latin America, analysts have said.

Portugal Telecom, whose profits soared 51 percent to 54.9 billion escudos ($319.4 million) in 1996, has already agreed a joint venture with Brazil's state-controlled Telebras to provide long-distance services in Brazil, Portugal and countries in Africa where Telecom already operates.
"It is very positive. It (Concert) is probably the strongest in commercial and marketing terms of the potential alliances," said Daniel Bennett of Lisbon broker M.Valores.
Concert fought off rival suits from the AT&T -led Unisource, which also includes Spain's Telefonica, and the Franco-German Global One alliance.

But it was still unclear whether the new alliance would face tough future competition from Telefonica in its bid to extend business in Latin America where the existing $36 billion dollar market is expected to nearly double to $60 billion by the end of the century.
Telefonica has been rumoured to be about to jump ship and agree to a link up between its international arm Telefonica Internacional and MCI.
An English version of the Portugal Telecom statement initially refered to its new alliance working together with a Pan American joint venture to be "announced...by MCI and Telefonica Internacional."
But the companies concerned subsequently said that the reference to a Spanish-U.S. deal was made in error. ($ = 171.9 Portugese Escudos)
